obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card compromise
trigger: Suspected or confirmed unauthorized access to card data or payment systems
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (contract term; fictional)
notify: Acquirer's risk line (Owner-Manager calls, then confirms in writing)

obligation: Visa notification of a compromise event
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, version 10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a payment system
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa, normally coordinated through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - card brand rule applied through the merchant agreement

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2 and Attachment A
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
notify: Visa, through the acquirer's upload tools

obligation: PCI Forensic Investigator (if Visa requires one)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Formal notice from Visa requiring a PFI investigation
deadline: Contract a PFI within 5 business days; preliminary report within 5 business days of contracting; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation
notify: Visa and the acquirer; the PFI must not have provided other services to the motel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if required by Visa (Visa may instead require an independent investigation, Section A.6)

obligation: Other card brands (Mastercard, American Express, Discover)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of that brand's account data
deadline: Per the brand's rules; timing not verified here. Follow the acquirer's instructions and treat 24 hours as the working target

trigger: Breach of security of electronic personal information of Florida residents. Includes a name with a card number and any required security code (keyed phone payments; emailed card forms) and a name with a driver license or ID card number (PMS ID scans) (501.171(1)(g)1.a.)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (unless delayed by law enforcement or waived under 501.171(4)(c)); 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the Department within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email, with the date range, the data involved, and a contact

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs, with a synopsis, the count, services offered, a copy of the individual notice, and a contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the motel reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if this path is used; counsel decides. Unlikely here: captured card numbers include security codes

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the motel (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the motel (PMS vendor, gateway, productivity suite vendor, backup service) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The motel (Assistant Manager and Owner-Manager); the motel then gives the 501.171(3) and (4) notices

trigger: Affected guests and crew members who reside outside Florida (most transient guests and many crew members)
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check residency of every affected person

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.3.3.4 (recommended)
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office (as named in the Visa document) or the FBI (IC3)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is considered for payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if extortion occurs. All U.S. persons

trigger: Suspected security incident or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the motel is far below the SBA size standard and lodging has no proposed sector criterion

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - Cris Santos Company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - Cris Santos Company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
